title: Multi-Dimensional Evaluation of Sustainable City Trips with LLM-as-a-Judge and Human-in-the-Loop

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing baseline LLM judgments across four dimensions (relevance, diversity, sustainability, and popularity mix) against human expert evaluations to identify systematic misalignments, idiosyncratic interpretations, and factual errors.

Analyzing directional preferences by calculating confidence-weighted aggregated scores (ASR) and best-list selections (BLR) between paired recommendation lists (L1 vs. L2) to identify if the judge systematically favors one position over the other.
Evaluating recommendation lists on a 'Popularity Mix' dimension to measure the balance between mainstream, widely known destinations and lesser-known alternatives to mitigate overtourism risks.
Using a structured pairwise comparison protocol instead of absolute rating scales to improve judgment stability and mitigate biases associated with absolute scoring.
